A Broken Song

Moira O’Neill (1864–1955)

W
HERE
 am I from?
 From the green hills of Erin.
Have I no song then?
 My songs are all sung.
What o’ my love?
 ’Tis alone I am farin’,
Old grows my heart, an’ my voice yet is young.
If she was tall?
 Like a king’s own daughter.
If she was fair?
 Like a mornin’ o’ May.
When she’d come laughin’ ’twas the runnin’ wather,
When she’d come blushin’ ’twas the break o’ day.
Where did she dwell?
 Where one’st I had my dwellin’.
Who loved her best?
 There ’s no one now will know.
Where is she gone?
 Och, why would I be tellin’!
Where she is gone there I can never go.
